A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of ProPhy, with matching architecture, equations, and main experiments. v1 includes Appendices A–D and Figures 9–14; the supplied v2 ends at the references and omits that material. This omission is directly observable, not an extraction gap.

before.justification: Tables 1–4 report original VideoPhy2 and VBench experiments and ablations. Appendix B additionally reports router analyses and a human assessment of annotation accuracy.

after.justification: Tables 1–4 retain original benchmark results and ablations, with qualitative experiments and expert analyses in Figures 5–8.

M1.justification: The SEB/PB/REB architecture, routing procedures, physical alignment strategy, and training objectives remain unchanged. Loss of appendix implementation details does not establish a change to the underlying method.

E1.justification: Both versions use WISA-80K for training and retain VideoPhy2 and VBench evaluation of physics-aware video generation. The omitted appendix diagnostics and examples do not establish a change in datasets, tasks, or represented domains.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain the same comparator membership, including WISA, VideoREPA, the backbone models, and the additional generators in Table 1. Newly cited PhysHPO and PISA are not evaluated. The omitted Figure 13 supplies further examples of existing comparisons.

E3.justification: The retained benchmark protocol still uses 600 prompts, the 180-prompt HARD subset, and the same metrics. Supplementary procedures disappear: PCA using 100 unseen prompts per phenomenon and a human annotation audit using 100 videos per phenomenon with four accuracy categories. No changed settings or reruns are established for retained experiments.

E4.justification: v2 omits Appendix B’s full-category semantic PCA, human validation of VLM annotations, comparison of short and elaborate annotation prompts, and qualitative SEB/REB ablations. These remove substantive checks of expert behavior and supervision quality, although the main ablation tables and expert visualizations remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, run-to-run variability, or significance tests. The omitted annotation-accuracy percentages are point results rather than uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 are numerically unchanged. v2 correctly attributes the 19.7% Joint improvement to CogVideoX, whose score rises from 22.3 to 26.7. However, substantial supplementary results disappear, including annotation accuracy of 76.9% overall, category accuracies of 63.1%, 87.7%, and 80.0%, inference overheads of 20.3% and 11.5%, and additional PCA and qualitative findings.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations and objectives in Equations 1–6 remain unchanged. Neither version presents theorems or proofs; omitted attention-extraction details concern implementation rather than revised mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction’s contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: progressive semantic and token-level physical experts, VLM-guided alignment, and improved physically plausible generation across backbones.

C2.justification: Section 4.5 reframes expert inversion from an ability to transfer physical attributes to evidence of distinct learned priors, with explicit attribute control presented as future potential. The main limitations paragraph survives, but appendix explanations of weaker dynamics annotations and dependence on VLM supervision disappear.

D1.justification: The omitted appendix contains crucial reproducibility information: PB layer choices, 32 experts and top-4 routing, training hardware and 8,000-step budget, optimizer and video settings, 50-step DDIM inference, annotation resizing and the 10% token cap, and refined-prompt selection. The code-release promise also disappears. v2 retains references to supplementary details without including them.

R1.justification: The introduction adds PhysHPO, PISA, and Lin et al.’s physics-cognition survey, and sharpens the distinction between internalizing priors during training and explicit guidance during inference. The broader related-work organization and positioning against global physical guidance remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Retained sections preserve their order and mostly their wording. Local edits affect the introduction, Figure 1 caption, and expert-inversion discussion; equal-contribution markings and an acknowledgment are added, contact text is removed, and the project link moves. The appendix block is omitted without substantial reorganization of the main narrative.

P2.justification: Figures 9–14 disappear, removing the PCA plot, annotation prompts and accuracy chart, qualitative ablation, and example galleries. Figures 1–2 receive labeling and diagram edits. Figure 4 moves and replaces one displayed video frame while retaining its heatmaps. The four main tables retain their structure.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects the 19.7% gain attribution, updates related work, and tempers the attribute-control interpretation. These useful refinements are outweighed by omission of the detailed implementation recipe and distinctive validation of annotation quality and expert behavior. The supplied later PDF substantially weakens reproducibility and supporting evidence while still directing readers to absent supplementary material.
